subject: MAP: EverCloud capacity plan & timelines for Dedicated/Private
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@evercloud.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: EverCloud capacity plan & timelines for Dedicated/Private

Maya —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, I put together an initial mutual action plan draft and a proposed cadence for evaluation -> pilot -> commit focused on Dedicated (cloud) and Private (VPC / on-prem) capacity. Highlights below; attached: MAP-draft-EverCloud-v1.pdf and gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx.

High-level proposal (we can tweak during the MAP sign-off):
- Evaluation sprint: 2 weeks (security review + 1-week integration sanity + perf runs) — target start: Oct 11
- Pilot / Canaries: 3 weeks (staging with real traffic, KV cache warmups) — target start: Oct 25
- Commit to Dedicated capacity: 60-day lead after signature (typical tranche provisioning in region)
- Private on-prem baseline: procurement + rack + network config ~10–14 weeks from PO (longer due to physical hardware & networking)

GPU pool sizing recommendation (initial -> steady):
- Starting tranche (decoupled): 6 x A100-equivalent for pilot (sized for 25 qps sustained at P99 SLA)
- Ramp to 12 x for production steady-state over 8 weeks (autoscale + burst through pooling)
- Contingency: 4x burst capacity via Hosted fallback to cover hardware lead delays

Acceptance criteria & gating:
- Pass perf benchmarks (P50/P95/P99) on representative prompt set (we'll publish prompt set v1)
- Security checklist: SOC2 evidence + network WPA config for VPC access
- Rollout plan: canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> full with automatic rollback policy on error rate > 1.5%

Key asks for EverCloud:
- Confirm procurement window (PO lead times / internal approval dates)
- Point person for SOC2 and procurement (procurement@evercloud.com is fine for now)
- Quick thumbs on the sizing sheet attached

If that looks reasonable, suggest we lock the evaluation start for Oct 11 — I can update the MAP PDF and circulate a DocuSign link for sign-off on the milestones.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: MAP-draft-EverCloud-v1.pdf [PDF], gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx [XLSX])

Subject: Re: MAP: EverCloud capacity plan & timelines for Dedicated/Private

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear plan and the sizing sheet. A few quick things from our side: 

1) Lead times: can you break down Dedicated (region-based) vs Private on-prem in a simple table? Our procurement team needs concrete calendar days to map to internal budget cycles.
2) Fallbacks: if there are supply delays for the on-prem GPUs, what does the hosted fallback look like operationally (SLA differences, data residency concerns)?
3) SOC2: we can share a contact in security, but can you attach the specific artifacts you mentioned (SOC2 report + evidence pointer)?
4) Contracting: procurement will need an MSA redline draft focused on capacity commits and optional termination windows — can you loop legal?

Procurement is copied (procurement@evercloud.com). We prefer evaluation start the week of Oct 11 but need to confirm with finance (we'll reply by EOD Wed).

-Maya
VP, Platform Engineering
EverCloud Inc

Subject: Re: MAP: EverCloud capacity plan & timelines for Dedicated/Private

Maya —

Thanks — answered inline below and attached a short leadtime-table.csv and a SOC2 evidence stub (soc2-evidence-stub.pdf) to accelerate your security review.

> 1) Lead times: can you break down Dedicated vs Private on-prem?
- Dedicated (cloud region, dedicated pool): typical tranche lead = 4–8 weeks from signed SOW/PO depending on region and available GPU inventory. We can ship smaller initial tranches (4-6 units) in 4 weeks and fill the remainder in the second tranche.
- Private on-prem (customer-managed): 10–14 weeks from PO for standard configs — this includes vendor procurement, rack provisioning, OS + network config, and onsite acceptance testing.

> 2) Fallbacks: hosted fallback operationally — SLA differences, data residency?
- Operationally: we can route a percentage of traffic to Redwood Hosted endpoints transparently (same API) while private hardware is being provisioned. Hosted fallback will have slightly different latency profiles and a separate tenancy with strict tenant isolation.
- Data residency: Hosted will live in the region you select (we can restrict to us-west-2). If contractual data residency prevents hosted fallback, we can do encrypted KV-only forwarding or delay ingress until private install. We'll add language for this to the MAP.

> 3) SOC2 artifacts?
- Attached: SOC2 summary and evidence pointers (soc2-evidence-stub.pdf). We can run an NDA / read-only link if you need deeper artifacts.

> 4) Contracting redlines?
- Looping in our legal via Marissa (cc'd) — Marissa, can you confirm a sample SOW template for capacity commit + termination windows we can prefill for EverCloud?

Suggested operational milestones (calendarized):
- Evaluation start: 2026-10-11 (2 weeks)
- Pilot start: 2026-10-25 (3 weeks)
- SOW sign & PO for Dedicated tranche: target 2026-11-29 (60-day lead)+(PO to ops)
- Private PO target: 2026-11-01 to stay within 10–14 week window for Jan production readiness

Contingency: if hardware delays extend Private lead beyond 14 weeks, we propose a hybrid model: Hosted fallback + temporary extended burst capacity while hardware is finalized (we'll cap cost and provide daily burn reports).

Attachments: leadtime-table.csv, soc2-evidence-stub.pdf

Let me know if you'd like a quick call tomorrow to walk procurement through the lead-time table.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: leadtime-table.csv [CSV], soc2-evidence-stub.pdf [PDF])

Looping in a small sizing tweak from infra: 
- Recommend initial pilot tranche be 6 x A100-equivalent (unchanged) but set burst pool to 4 x (instead of 6) with autoscale rules tuned to 60% CPU/KV-util threshold. This reduces initial commitment while giving the pilot headroom.

Karthik — please confirm the updated numbers make sense for EverCloud's 25 qps P99 target. Marissa — can you start a draft SOW with both options (6+4 burst vs 8 steady) to give procurement flexibility?

Thanks,
Grace
Director, Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference
